observation_summary: The Mockito framework fails to correctly identify and match method calls on a mocked object when the object is cast to a super-interface (e.g., casting MyIterable to Iterable). The stubbing and verification fail because the framework does not correctly associate the method signature of the sub-interface with the method signature of the super-interface.
reasoning_summary: The issue is that Mockito's internal mechanism for tracking method invocations fails to recognize that a method call on a sub-interface (MyIterable) is equivalent to the same method call on its super-interface (Iterable). This is a classic case of a broken association between related structures (the interface hierarchy and the method invocation tracking), where the framework needs to maintain consistency between these related types to correctly identify the method being called or verified.
evidence_gaps: The internal implementation of the method matching logic in Mockito is not provided, only the test case demonstrating the failure.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While it involves an interface, the core issue is not a mismatch in the signature itself, but the framework's failure to maintain the relationship/equivalence between the sub-interface method and the super-interface method during invocation tracking.
The failure is not due to a local computational error, but rather a failure to correctly associate two related interface types in the mock tracking system.
